newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cenbank eyes more control of Brazil banks abroad.
newsitem.headline: Cenbank eyes more control of Brazil banks abroad.

text.p: The Central Bank will discuss with foreign central banks and regulators ways to tighten supervision of Brazilian banks abroad, Central Bank chief Gustavo Loyola was quoted as saying.

Loyola's comments to Gazeta Mercantil newspaper come after a recent resolution by National Monetary Council (CMN) which allowed the Central Bank to request banks with branches abroad to disclose information on their activities as of January 1997.
Gazeta said the Central Bank already notified all Brazilian bank branches abroad of the CMN's resolution.

Brazil's banking supervision was thrust to center stage recently following revelations of irregularities, including alleged fraud, at failed banks Banco Nacional and Banco Economico. The two were among the country's top 10 banks.
